queen-mary.name: QUEEN MARY (liner)

manhattan.name: MANHATTAN, WASHINGTON (liners; USS Wakefield AP-21, USS Mount Vernon AP-22)
manhattan.plate: ONI 208, Merchant Ship Recognition Manual, 21 Apr 1942, p. 41 (M-F-F-M, profile "Manhattan, Washington"; index: MANHATTAN, American, 1932, TG, 24,289 GT, p. 41; Internet Archive leaf 0083). Masts and kingposts are added back upright at their positions, to their trucks as drawn. Drawn as the liner the plate shows: USS Wakefield (AP-21, ex-Manhattan) and USS Mount Vernon (AP-22, ex-Washington) carried guns, gun tubs and extra cargo booms in the war (the Journal of Recognition, January 1944, p. 11, leaf n6 of USANJOR194401, photographs Wakefield with booms at both masts and gun tubs aft), which this outline does not show. Mirrored to put the bow on the right (the plate draws the bow on the left)

victory.name: VC2 (VICTORY) cargo ship
victory.plate: ONI 222-US, 1 Sep 1945, p. 183 (PDF p. 204): BOULDER VICTORY Class (AK 227-236, BOULDER VICTORY to LAKEWOOD VICTORY), statistical summary length 455' (oa), beam 62', draft 28' (max), completed 1944; photograph of AK 230 MANDERSON VICTORY, 1945, on p. 184. Traced from the profile (rendered at 400 dpi; threshold 160, opened 4 px to drop the stays and booms, the waterline levelled by 0.33 degrees) and scaled to the printed length. The plate's own 0-60 ft height scale does not agree with that length: read on it, every height is about 1.56 times lower (the funnel top 42 ft, not 67 ft). Scaled to the length, as the other entries are, the funnel and kingposts come within a few feet of the LIBERTY's (ONI 208, measured on its scale bar). The kingposts, the posts at each end of the house, the mast over the funnel and the foremast, thinned away by the opening, are drawn back as masts at the plate's positions to their tops as drawn. This is the Navy's fit: a 5"/38 aft and a 3"/50 forward in gun tubs, with 40 mm and 20 mm mounts; a merchant Victory's Armed Guard guns stood in the same places, but no plate of a merchant or troop-carrying Victory was found

ning-hai.name: NING HAI class PG (ex-Chinese cruisers NING HAI, PING HAI)

Lists NING HAI (PG 8) and PING HAI (PG 9): "captured from the Chinese in 1937 ... New names, armament unknown. Note differences in aft deckhouse arrangement. Profile is of NING HAI." Drawn as built, before PING HAI's rebuilding as the escort YASOJIMA (ONI 222-J, June 1945, lists YASOJIMA as a light cruiser, ex-escort, p. VI (scan leaf 12), and NING HAI and PING HAI among the available non-Japanese warships, p. XI (scan leaf 17); it has no plate of either). Traced from the profile (blurred 1.2 px, threshold 225; the height lines, the frame and the base rule erased) at 2.21 px/ft (first scaled to the printed 360', against 2.17 px/ft from the height lines, within 2%), then traced again at the same scale without the derrick boom off the mainmast tripod and the plate's frame line at the bow, which the first trace kept: 357 ft overall, within 1% of the printed length; the lines read the foremast top about 101', the trace 100'. Bow already to the right
ning-hai.detail_note: the ONI 41-42 plate is tone-shaded with stipple; no dark key lines inside the outline
